topic: Can the filter's suppression of 19th harmonics improve transponder power efficiency in dense payload configurations?
response: Filter suppression of 19th harmonics can improve transponder power efficiency in dense payload configurations by reducing intermodulation products (IMDs) caused by nonlinear amplifier operation. IMDs contribute to intersymbol interference (ISI) and adjacent channel interference (ACI), leading to signal degradation and reduced power efficiency.  Filtering techniques, such as those used in the Owls paper, can mitigate these effects.
reference_context: The Owls paper describes a receiver design using 4-element passive LC filters for incoherently demodulating ASK signals. These filters minimize harmonic contents on the subcarrier frequencies, leading to channel separation and reduced interference. This approach demonstrates the effectiveness of filtering techniques in improving power efficiency.
